Furlong
FUR-long
n.
Old English furlang, “furrow-long,” the length of a furrow in a field; in modern terms, one-eighth of a mile (220 yards / 201 meters). The KJV uses furlong for the Greek stadion, the standard Greco-Roman unit of approximately 600 feet / 185 meters.

📖 Biblical Definition

The furlong (Greek stadion) is the standard Greco-Roman unit of distance used across the New Testament for the measurement of distances between places, the dimensions of large objects, and (most strikingly) the dimensions of the New Jerusalem in Revelation 21. Several biblical uses anchor the doctrine. First, the distance-from-Jerusalem of various NT events. Luke 24:13: the village of Emmaus, to which the two disciples were walking on the day of Christ’s resurrection, was threescore furlongs (60 stadia, approximately 7 miles) from Jerusalem. John 6:19: the disciples in the boat at the storm-on-the-lake had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs (25-30 stadia, approximately 3-3.5 miles) when they saw Jesus walking on the water. John 11:18: Bethany, where Lazarus was raised, was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off (15 stadia, approximately 2 miles). Each gives the precise distance for the historical-narrative reader. Second, the dimensions of large-scale eschatological objects. Revelation 14:20 records the bloody outcome of the apocalyptic harvest: and the winepress was trodden without the city, and blood came out of the winepress, even unto the horse bridles, by the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs—1,600 stadia (approximately 200 miles), an immense extent representing the comprehensive nature of the eschatological judgment. Third, and supremely, the dimensions of the New Jerusalem. Revelation 21:16: and the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal. The New Jerusalem is described as a perfect cube of 12,000 stadia per side—approximately 1,500 miles per side, an immense city echoing the perfect-cube-shape of the most holy place in tabernacle and temple (which was a 10-cubit cube in the tabernacle, 20-cubit cube in Solomon’s temple). The New Jerusalem is, in its very dimensions, the consummate holy of holies: the place where God’s presence dwells perfectly with His people, with no temple in the city because the LORD God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. The 12,000-stadia measurement is therefore not numerical decoration but the consummate eschatological architectural figure of the perfect dwelling-place of God with His redeemed. The furlong as a biblical unit therefore serves both the historical-narrative function (precise distances for events) and the apocalyptic-eschatological function (the immense dimensions of the consummate city).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines FURLONG as a measure of length, the eighth of a mile; in scripture, the KJV renders the Greek stadion as furlong, used for distances (Emmaus 60 furlongs from Jerusalem) and for the immense dimensions of the New Jerusalem (12,000 furlongs per side, Rev 21:16).

FURLONG, n. — A measure of length; the eighth of a mile; forty rods, poles, or perches. In scripture, the KJV renders the Greek stadion as furlong; the standard Greco-Roman unit of approximately 600 feet.

STADION (Greek) — The standard Greco-Roman unit of distance, approximately 600 feet / 185 meters; named for the stadia of the Greek athletic games.

📖 Key Scripture

Luke 24:13 — "And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs."

John 11:18 — "Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off."

Revelation 14:20 — "And the winepress was trodden without the city, and blood came out of the winepress, even unto the horse bridles, by the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs."

Revelation 21:16 — "And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The furlong-doctrine is corrupted, on one side, by the modern translation drift that has substituted miles or stadia for the KJV’s furlong—and on the other (more significantly) by the over-spiritualization of the Revelation 21:16 dimensions of the New Jerusalem that treats the 12,000 furlongs as merely symbolic without the substantive architectural-eschatological connection to the holy-of-holies-as-perfect-cube pattern Scripture itself maintains.

expand to see more

Modern translations have variously rendered stadion as mile (approximate equivalent), stadia (Greek transliteration), or specific-distance equivalents (two miles off for the 15 stadia of John 11:18). Each has its rationale; each loses something the KJV’s furlong preserves: the precise unit-name that lets the reader track the specific measurements as the biblical writers gave them. The furlong-precision matters especially in Revelation, where the apocalyptic visions use specific numerical figures (the 1,600 furlongs of Rev 14:20; the 12,000 furlongs of Rev 21:16) that are themselves part of the symbolic substance the visions convey. The recovery is the recovery of attention to the precise units, with the modern reader paying enough attention to the numerical detail to engage the symbolic substance the apocalyptic-and-narrative measurements carry.

The deeper substance is the New-Jerusalem-as-consummate-holy-of-holies pattern Revelation 21:16 conveys. The city is described as a perfect cube of 12,000 furlongs per side—immensely larger than any earthly city, and significantly cube-shaped, with length, breadth, and height equal. The cube-shape echoes the holy of holies of the tabernacle (a perfect 10-cubit cube, Ex 26:33 by inference; Lev 16:14-15 in priestly use) and of Solomon’s temple (a perfect 20-cubit cube, 1 Kgs 6:20: and the oracle in the forepart was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in the height thereof). The consummate New Jerusalem of Rev 21 is therefore the eschatological holy of holies—the perfect dwelling-place of God with His redeemed, no longer a small inner room in a larger sanctuary but the entire city, into which the redeemed enter and where the LORD God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple. The furlong-measurements of 12,000 per side, and the explicit length and breadth and height of it are equal, are the architectural-symbolic figures the apocalyptic vision uses to convey the consummate eschatological reality: the holy of holies expanded to encompass the entire city of God’s redeemed people, with no veil, no separation, no inaccessible inner chamber—only the perpetual presence of God with His people in the perfect-cube city forever.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English furlang (furrow-long); KJV rendering of the Greek stadion, the standard Greco-Roman unit of approximately 600 feet; used for NT distances (Emmaus, Bethany, the storm-on-the-lake) and for the immense apocalyptic dimensions of the New Jerusalem (12,000 furlongs per side, perfect cube, Rev 21:16) echoing the holy of holies of tabernacle and temple.

expand to see more

Greek stadion (G4712) — furlong, stadia (7 NT uses).

Old English furlang — furrow-long, the length of a field-furrow.

Hebrew unit equivalent: no exact OT equivalent; the LXX uses stadion for various OT distance-measurements.

Greek stadios-cognate — standing, fixed (the etymological root, referring to the standardized fixed length of the Greek athletic stadion track).

Usage

"Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs—Luke 24:13’s precise distance of the resurrection-day road."

"The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal—Rev 21:16’s perfect-cube New Jerusalem of 12,000 furlongs per side, echoing the holy of holies of tabernacle and temple."

"Modern translations flatten the furlong-precision; recovery is attention to the specific numerical figures, especially in the apocalyptic visions where the measurements carry symbolic substance."
